request_evidence.title: llama.cpp v0.8.0
request_evidence.evidence: ## Overview This release adds the LiquidAI LFM3 family (text, vision, audio and omni) together with a new experimental streaming-audio API in `mtmd`, and wires realtime audio in and out of the server through the new `/v1/realtime` and `/tts` endpoints. A batch of new architectures landed: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, SenseNova U1, Beam, Kolibri-1, Flint, Muse Spark, Granite Switch Decision, plus decision/embedding models from LiquidAI, Baidu and NVIDIA. The core got sparse-attention (QSA/DSA) reworked onto a fused masking op, a 50/50 SLRU cache for host-resident MoE experts, and cleaner `no_alloc` memory handling; the server got router memory-management and tool-calling improvements; the UI can now browse and download models straight from HF Hub, search conversations and compact them. Finally, `ggml` was bumped to v0.28.0, bringing `GGML_OP_TOP_K_MASK`, `-1` expert-index semantics and large backend performance work (CUDA chunked graph launches, SYCL graph replay, OpenCL Q2_K/Q3_K, Hexagon HTP rework, KleidiAI SVE kernels). ### Highlights - LFM3 family: LFM3-1.7B (text) and LFM3-VL-2B (vision), verified against the reference HF implementation [llama/31252](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.

Super-agent Over the past year, coding agents and other single-task agents have shown that models can use tools to solve complex problems while needing less and less continuous monitoring and step-by-step intervention from humans. Models have also become better at coordinating multiple agents, which makes it practical to organize and schedule work across sessions. As people take less part in low-level execution, their role is gradually moving up to higher-level decisions and sign-off. Better models have also enabled new applications. request_evidence.evidence: GitHub Copilot Fusion is generally available. Instead of picking a model for each task, choose Copilot Fusion and let Copilot intelligently route and orchestrate which models it uses for you. Copilot Fusion brings together Project HydraFusion’s multi-model orchestration and Copilot auto model selection’s fine-tuned model selection, leveraging the benefits of both to balance performance and cost efficiency. Since Project HydraFusion launched, we’ve improved its performance. In the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, Copilot Fusion Max scored 60, within two points of Claude Code with Opus 5.5 Max. It delivered that result at about half the average API cost per task, using about half as many tokens and taking about 40% less time per task. Smarter choices for developers When you select Copilot Fusion in the model picker, you aren’t selecting a specific model. You’re choosing a system that routes and orchestrates models for each task. request_evidence.evidence: Show HN: Bowerbird – Open-source NotebookLM for any model, with checked quotes PRIMARY PAGE: # Bowerbird An open-source NotebookLM alternative where your files stay yours and every quote is checked. Add PDFs, books, web pages, YouTube videos and recordings, then ask questions. Answers cite the passages they draw on, and each quoted phrase is looked up in the source it cites. Notebooks are plain folders on your disk, search, OCR and speech run on your machine, and answers come from any model you choose. ![An answer about the Peace of Westphalia, with cited quotes in the margin](docs/screenshots/answer.png) ## Every quote is checked Each citation in an answer carries the words it quotes. Bowerbird looks those words up in the source the citation names: in the cited passage, or in another passage of the same source, since a quote can run across a passage boundary. A quote that isn't there, or that the answer attributes to the wrong source, is marked unverified, and the footer counts how many were found. A quote shortened with an ellipsis counts only when each of its pieces is long enough to stand on
